component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Compiled selected adversarial C++ programs with g++ (C++20, -Wall -Wextra, and -Wconversion) inside the sandbox and captured raw compiler diagnostic text as evidence. | C++ compiler diagnostics (GCC) are excellent for syntax errors (precise location, caret, contextual notes) but structurally weak for silent semantic hazards like integer narrowing, which require opt-in flags and remain non-fatal warnings even when enabled. No mandatory sound type/borrow checking exists at the language level (unlike Rust) to catch this class of bug at compile time by default. Score set to 58/100 reflecting strong syntactic diagnostics offset by weak default detection of a broad class of real-world numeric correctness bugs. | Diagnostics are precise (line/column caret), include a helpful note pointing back to the unmatched brace, and separately flag unused-variable/statement-has-no-effect. Good syntax-error locality and secondary notes, but cascading errors from one truncation point produced two separate error messages requiring correlation by the reader. | g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -c adv22a.cpp -o adv22a.o | adversarial/ADV-22a_single.cpp (truncated/malformed statement) | adv22a.cpp:7:14: error: expected ';' at end of input ... adv22a.cpp:7:14: error: expected '}' at end of input ... note: to match this '{' ... warning: statement has no effect [-Wunused-value] ... warning: unused variable 'v'…

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Qualitative assessment of C++20 language feature coverage exercised against the assigned adversarial/micro corpus (templates, RAII, operator overloading, constexpr, concepts, std:: containers/algorithms, exception handling, multi-paradigm support via lambdas). | Corpus (template/programs/cpp/adversarial, .../micro) exercises integer overflow/narrowing (ADV-01), UB edge cases, recursion depth (ADV-21 variants), and malformed-syntax negative cases (ADV-22a/b), showing the language supports low-level numeric control needed for systems-level expressiveness. | C++ offers rich expressiveness: templates/generics with concepts, operator overloading, RAII-based resource management, multiple inheritance, lambdas/closures, coroutines (C++20), constexpr metaprogramming, and a large standard library (algorithm, ranges, containers). | Weaknesses versus more modern languages: no native sum types/pattern matching (workarounds via std::variant + std::visit are verbose), manual memory-safety discipline required (raw pointers, lifetime bugs still expressible), macro preprocessor is a blunt, non-hygienic metaprogramming tool, and template error surfaces (pre-concepts) are historically very verbose (mitigated but not eliminated by C++20 concepts). | Score reflects a mature, extremely expressive but syntactically heavy language with excellent low-level control paired with only partial adoption of mo…
